common.confirm_clear: Clear all values in this section?
common.confirm_defaults: Reset this section to default values?

service.not_installed_body: Install Caddy to use this plugin. On most distros: sudo pacman -S caddy / sudo apt install caddy / sudo dnf install caddy
service.api_unreachable_body: Caddy is not running or the Admin API is not enabled. Start Caddy to continue.
service.unit_failed_body: systemd reports the caddy service as failed — it may have started and then immediately crashed (for example, if something else is already using its configured port).
service.unmanaged_body: The Admin API is reachable, but not confirmed to be served by a local, actively-running systemd service — it may be running in a container, or some other process may be using the same port/socket. Proxy management, the Caddyfile editor, and logs all work through the Admin API and a configured container name, but Start/Stop/Restart are disabled here, since they could target the wrong process.
service.confirm_start_body: This will start the Caddy reverse proxy service.
service.confirm_stop_body: This will stop Caddy and take down all reverse proxies.
service.confirm_restart_body: Caddy will restart, briefly interrupting all active connections.
service.confirm_reload_body: Caddy will reload its configuration without interrupting existing connections.

proxies.title: Reverse Proxies
proxies.empty_body: Add a proxy to expose a local service over HTTPS.
proxies.service_not_running: Start the Caddy service to view and manage proxies.
proxies.delete_confirm_body: This will remove the reverse proxy for port {{port}} → {{target}}.
proxies.api_error_add_title: Proxy created on disk — Caddy rejected the live push
proxies.api_error_edit_title: Label saved — Caddy rejected the config update (other changes not applied)
proxies.caddyfile_error_title: Caddyfile validation failed — changes not saved
proxies.raw_blocks_help: This site has route or nested handle blocks. The Tree tab edits them; what it shows as raw is edited in the raw editor.
proxies.raw_blocks_notice: This site has route or nested handle blocks. The form leaves them as written and only changes the site's address, bind, imports and TLS. Edit the blocks in the Tree tab; what it shows as raw is edited in the raw editor.

add_proxy.title: Add Reverse Proxy
add_proxy.field_external_address_help: Protocol and hostname are optional. Port is required. Separate several hostnames with commas.
add_proxy.ext_host_placeholder: hostname, or several separated by commas (optional)
add_proxy.validation_ext_host_required_with_scheme: Hostname is required when a protocol is set
add_proxy.validation_ext_host_empty_entry: There is an empty entry in the hostname list. Remove the extra comma.
add_proxy.validation_ext_host_space: "{{host}}" contains a space. Separate hostnames with commas; a hostname can't contain spaces.
add_proxy.validation_ext_host_scheme_or_port: "{{host}}" includes a protocol or port. Enter hostnames only and set the protocol and port in their own fields.
add_proxy.validation_https_requires_tls: The "https" protocol requires TLS to be enabled below — Caddy would otherwise manage HTTPS on its own, ungoverned by this app's settings. Enable TLS or choose a different protocol.
add_proxy.field_tls_skip_verify: Skip TLS verification on backend (for self-signed backend certs)
add_proxy.validation_target_port_range: Target port must be between 1 and 65535
add_proxy.confirm_body: This will create a reverse proxy :{{port}} → {{target}} and reload Caddy's configuration.
add_proxy.field_label_help: A name for this site in the list, e.g. Grafana.

add_static.title: Add Static File Server
add_static.field_root_help: Path on disk to serve files from
add_static.confirm_body: This will create a static file server on :{{port}} serving {{root}} and reload Caddy's configuration.
add_static.field_spa: SPA mode (serve index.html for unknown paths)
add_static.field_spa_help: For single-page apps (React, Vue, Svelte builds): existing files are served as they are, every other path gets index.html so deep links work.
add_static.field_index_help: File names tried for a directory, separated by spaces, in order.
add_static.field_hide_help: Names or patterns that are never served, separated by spaces.
add_static.field_precompressed_help: Serve file.zst, file.br or file.gz next to the original when the browser accepts that encoding.
add_static.field_browse_template_help: A template file for the directory listing. Only used when directory listing is on.
add_static.field_status_help: Answer every file with this status code instead of 200, for example 404 for a custom error page.
add_static.field_disable_canonical_uris: Keep trailing slashes as they are
add_static.field_disable_canonical_uris_help: Do not redirect to add or remove a trailing slash on directories and files.
add_static.field_templates_help: Turns on Caddy's template engine for the served files, so they can use include, .Req and the other template actions.
add_static.field_templates_root_help: Where include and the other file actions look for files. Empty means the site root.

edit_static.title: Edit Static Server — :{{port}}
edit_static.confirm_body: This will update the static file server on :{{port}} and reload Caddy's configuration.

php_fastcgi.add_confirm_body: This will create a PHP site on :{{port}} and reload Caddy's configuration.
php_fastcgi.edit_confirm_body: This will update the PHP site on :{{port}} and reload Caddy's configuration.
php_fastcgi.field_upstream_help: Unix socket (e.g. unix//run/php-fpm.sock) or TCP address (127.0.0.1:9000) of the PHP-FPM process.
php_fastcgi.field_split_path_help: Extensions used to split the URI into script path and path info. Space-separated. Leave blank for Caddy's own default (.php).
php_fastcgi.field_try_files_help: Optional. Candidates tried in order before PHP; a front-controller app usually needs {path} {path}/ /index.php?{query}.
php_fastcgi.field_capture_stderr_help: Write what PHP-FPM prints to its stderr into Caddy's log.
php_fastcgi.field_resolve_root_symlink_help: Follow symlinks in the root directory before SCRIPT_FILENAME is built, which opcache setups with release symlinks need.

add_respond.title: Add Static Response
add_respond.field_body_help: Plain text or HTML response body. Leave empty for no body.
add_respond.validation_status_range: Status code must be between 100 and 599
add_respond.confirm_body: This will create a static response on :{{port}} returning HTTP {{status}} and reload Caddy's configuration.

edit_respond.title: Edit Response — :{{port}}
edit_respond.confirm_body: This will update the static response on :{{port}} to HTTP {{status}} and reload Caddy's configuration.

add_redirect.title: Add Redirect
add_redirect.shortcut_http_https_help: Listens on :80, redirects all traffic to https://{host}{uri} with a 308
add_redirect.confirm_body: This will create a redirect on :{{port}} → {{to}} ({{code}}) and reload Caddy's configuration.
add_redirect.code_html_help: Answers with a page that redirects in the browser instead of a status code. Unlike a status code redirect, it keeps the #fragment of the URL.
add_redirect.keep_path_help: Adds {uri} to the target, so /a?b=1 on this site goes to /a?b=1 on the target.

basic_auth.heading: HTTP Basic Auth
basic_auth.algorithm_mismatch: Accounts that keep their password still have a hash made with the other algorithm. Enter their passwords again.

transport.heading: Upstream Timeouts
transport.defaults_help: Leave a field empty to use Caddy's default, shown greyed out. A response header timeout cuts off long polling and slow responses.
transport.streaming_help: Streaming (websockets, event streams): leave empty to keep Caddy's defaults.

server_timeouts.heading: Server Timeouts & Limits
server_timeouts.defaults_help: Leave a field empty to use Caddy's default, shown greyed out. A read body or write timeout ends every upload or download that takes longer.
server_timeouts.max_header_bytes_help: Maximum request header size (Caddy's default: 16 KB)
server_timeouts.http3_help: Caddy enables HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 by default whenever TLS is configured. HTTP/3 runs over UDP on the same port as HTTPS — if UDP is blocked by your firewall, disabling it here falls back to HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 only.
server_timeouts.strict_sni_host_help: Reject requests whose Host header differs from the TLS server name.
server_timeouts.log_credentials_help: Write the Authorization and Cookie headers to the access log.
server_timeouts.enable_full_duplex_help: Let a handler read the request body while it writes the response.

request_body.field_help: Larger request bodies are rejected before they reach the backend. Leave empty for no limit (Caddy's default).

rewrite.heading: URI Rewrite
rewrite.invalid: Fill in every field of the rewrite.

probe.confirm_body: Every 5 seconds, cockpit-caddy will probe each proxy's upstream with an HTTP request (5 s connect timeout, 10 s max). Any HTTP response — even 4xx/5xx — counts as reachable; connection refused or timeout shows the upstream as down. Probing stops as soon as you disable the toggle.

upstreams.heading: Additional Upstreams
upstreams.policy_default_help: Caddy picks an upstream at random.
upstreams.policy_random_help: Picks an upstream at random for each request.
upstreams.policy_least_conn_help: Picks the upstream with the fewest open requests.
upstreams.policy_first_help: Always the first available upstream in the list; the others are fallbacks.
upstreams.policy_weighted_round_robin_help: Takes the upstreams in turn, each as often as its weight; weight 0 takes one out.
upstreams.policy_random_choose_help: Picks n upstreams at random and uses the least busy of them.
upstreams.policy_ip_hash_help: The same connection IP always reaches the same upstream.
upstreams.policy_client_ip_hash_help: Like the connection IP hash, but uses the real client IP behind trusted proxies.
upstreams.policy_uri_hash_help: The same request path always reaches the same upstream, good for caches.
upstreams.policy_header_help: The value of a request header picks the upstream; the same value always reaches the same one.
upstreams.policy_cookie_help: Sticky sessions: Caddy sets a cookie on the first response, and later requests with it reach the same upstream.
upstreams.field_cookie_secret_help: Optional. Signs the cookie value, so clients can't pick an upstream themselves.
upstreams.validation_weights: Enter one whole-number weight for each of the {{count}} upstreams.
upstreams.validation_choose: Enter a whole number of at least 1.

lb_retry.heading: Retry & Failover Tuning
lb_retry.passive_help: Upstream responses with these codes count as failures. Passive checks only run with a fail duration: an upstream that reaches max fails within it is taken out of rotation for that long.
lb_retry.active_help: Caddy requests this path on every upstream at the interval and takes upstreams that fail out of rotation. Leave the path empty to turn active checks off.
lb_retry.validation_needs_fail_duration: Unhealthy status codes and max fails only take effect with a fail duration
lb_retry.validation_max_fails: Max fails must be 1 or greater
lb_retry.validation_needs_health_uri: Interval, timeout and expected status need a health check path
lb_retry.validation_health_uri: The health check path must start with /
lb_retry.validation_health_status: Use a status code like 200 or a class like 2xx
lb_retry.validation_methods: Methods are words like GET or HEAD, separated by spaces.

edit_redirect.title: Edit Redirect — :{{port}}
edit_redirect.confirm_body: This will update the redirect on :{{port}} and reload Caddy's configuration.

edit_proxy.title: Edit Proxy — :{{port}}
edit_proxy.confirm_save_body: This will update the proxy on :{{port}} and reload Caddy's configuration.

caddyfile.saved_needs_reload: File saved — reload Caddy to apply changes
caddyfile.managed_file: The Proxy List tab reads and writes this file directly. Saving a proxy there rewrites the block that holds it (for a route on a named server, that server's whole block), so hand edits inside that block can be replaced. Other blocks are left as they are.
caddyfile.unmanaged_note: This is the Caddyfile on the host filesystem. Whether it's the file the running container actually reads depends on how that container is configured (shared bind mount vs. its own separate config) — edits here may have no effect on the live instance unless the container shares this path.

logs.no_matches: No log lines match your search.
logs.container_not_configured: Caddy is running externally. Set a container name in Admin API Address settings (gear icon) to view its logs.

migration.banner_body: The sites in your Caddyfile will move to the plugin's conf.d file so it can manage them.
migration.confirm_body: All proxy entries will be moved verbatim to /etc/caddy/conf.d/cockpit-caddy.conf and /etc/caddy/Caddyfile will be replaced with an import statement. The original is backed up to /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.bak. Caddy will reload automatically.
migration.gate_body: Your proxies are defined directly in /etc/caddy/Caddyfile. This plugin writes to /etc/caddy/conf.d — without migrating first, Caddy may see duplicate server entries and reject the configuration.
migration.gate_continue_warning: Continuing without migration may cause Caddy to reject the configuration due to duplicate entries.
migration.backup_warning_body: Migration only backs up the Caddyfile itself. Create a full config backup so you can restore everything if something goes wrong.
migration.banner_details: Site blocks move unchanged from /etc/caddy/Caddyfile to /etc/caddy/conf.d/cockpit-caddy.conf, and the Caddyfile gets an import line for conf.d. The original Caddyfile is backed up to /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.bak. Until then, the plugin's changes may clash with the sites in the Caddyfile.

backup.title: Backup Caddy Config
backup.warning_partial: Archive created with warnings (some files may have changed during backup)

restore.title: Restore Caddy Config
restore.no_archives: No caddy-config-*.tar.gz files found in this directory.
restore.success_body: Caddy configuration has been restored. Reload Caddy to apply.
restore.needs_reload_body: The restored config is on disk but Caddy is still running the old config. Reload to apply the changes.

admin.warning_body: This plugin manages system services and configuration files. Without administrative access in Cockpit, most actions will fail. Enable administrative mode in the top-right Cockpit menu before continuing.

access_log.heading: Access logging
access_log.file_path_required: File path is required when output is File
access_log.file_path_help: Must be writable by the caddy service. This plugin automatically fixes file ownership after each save, so a brand-new path should just work — but if Caddy still can't write here after saving, check that the parent directory itself is writable by the caddy user.
access_log.roll_help: Caddy rotates the log file by default. Leave a field empty to use Caddy's default, shown greyed out.
access_log.field_filters_help: One per line: a field path, then delete, hash, replace <text> or ip_mask <IPv4 bits> [<IPv6 bits>], for example request>headers>Authorization delete.
access_log.field_filters_invalid: Each line needs a field path and one of delete, hash, replace <text> or ip_mask <bits>.
access_log.include_help: Logger names this log writes, space-separated, for example http.log.access. Empty means all.
access_log.exclude_help: Logger names this log skips, space-separated, for example http.log.access.log0.
access_log.skip_paths: Paths to leave out of the log
access_log.skip_paths_help: Space-separated paths, wildcards allowed, for example /health* /ping. Requests to them are not logged.

config_check.title: Check Config
config_check.intro: This scans the Caddyfile and conf.d for known-stale configuration shapes — each one traced to a specific reason Caddy would refuse to reload. Review each finding's before/after and explanation, then choose which fixes to apply. This is safe to run at any time, including while the config is currently broken.
config_check.load_error: Could not read the current configuration.
config_check.no_issues: No issues found — the configuration looks correct.
config_check.apply_error: Failed to apply — changes not saved
config_check.apply_ok: Fixes applied. Reload Caddy for them to take effect.
config_check.cert_issuer_title: Replace the old global certificate-lifetime directive
config_check.cert_issuer_explanation: An older version of this plugin wrote the shared internal-issuer lifetime as a real Caddy directive (`cert_issuer`). Caddy rejects that as soon as any proxy without a hostname also sets its own certificate lifetime — it sees two different definitions of the same default certificate policy and refuses to reload ("automation policy from site block is also default/catch-all policy ... in conflict"). The value ({{lifetime}}) is kept, just stored safely as a comment instead, which Caddy ignores.
config_check.http_scheme_explanation: Caddy only excludes a site from its automatic-HTTPS bookkeeping when the address explicitly says "http://" — a bare address is still eligible even with TLS off in this app, and can silently claim the shared internal-issuer policy with no certificate settings at all, which then conflicts with any other hostless proxy that has an explicit lifetime.
config_check.lifetime_drift_title: Sync {{target}} to the shared certificate lifetime
config_check.lifetime_drift_explanation: This has no hostname, so it must use the exact same internal-issuer lifetime as every other hostless proxy/server — Caddy allows only one shared policy for all of them. It currently has {{current}}, but the shared value is {{shared}}.

global_opts.title: Global Caddy options
global_opts.caddyfile_note: These settings are written to the global options block in /etc/caddy/Caddyfile. Caddy is reloaded automatically on save.
global_opts.unmanaged_hint: No explicit global options are set — Caddy is using its automatic HTTPS defaults (including Let's Encrypt when a proxy has a public hostname). The fields below are empty because nothing needs to be configured, not because anything is broken.
global_opts.debug_help: Raises the global log level to DEBUG. Produces very verbose output.
global_opts.confirm_body: This will overwrite the global options section in /etc/caddy/Caddyfile. A Caddy reload will be required to apply the changes.
global_opts.needs_reload: Caddyfile updated — reload Caddy to apply the new global options
global_opts.save_error: Caddyfile validation failed — changes not saved
global_opts.validation_port: Must be a port number between 1 and 65535
global_opts.save_ok: Settings saved — reload Caddy to apply
global_opts.acme_note: ACME requires servers to have an explicit hostname in their external address (e.g. proxy.example.com). Servers with only a port (e.g. :443) and internal CA enabled create a catch-all TLS policy that conflicts with global ACME. ACME is only useful when your server is publicly reachable on port 80 or 443.
global_opts.acme_email_help: Required by Let's Encrypt and most ACME providers for expiry notifications.
global_opts.acme_ca_help: Leave blank to use the default (Let's Encrypt production). Select a preset or enter a custom URL.
global_opts.acme_ca_root_help: Path to a PEM file of trusted root certificates for connecting to the ACME CA server. Only needed for private/custom CAs.
global_opts.acme_eab_help: External Account Binding credentials required by some providers (e.g. ZeroSSL). Both fields must be set together.
global_opts.on_demand_enabled_help: Sets the endpoint Caddy asks before it gets a certificate on demand. This doesn't turn on-demand TLS on: that is a per-site option in each site's HTTPS settings.
global_opts.on_demand_no_ask_warning: No ask URL set — Caddy will issue certificates for any domain without authorization. Set an ask URL to prevent abuse.
global_opts.on_demand_ask_help: Caddy queries this endpoint before issuing a certificate. It must return HTTP 2xx to allow issuance.
global_opts.internal_tls_note: Caddy can only scope a certificate policy by hostname. Proxies/servers with no hostname all share this one setting — there's no way to give two hostless proxies different lifetimes. Proxies with a real hostname can still set their own in the TLS Policy section of their edit dialog.
global_opts.internal_cert_lifetime_help: How long internal-issuer certificates on hostless proxies/servers stay valid before renewal (Caddy default: 12h). Use a Caddy duration, e.g. 90d, 365d (Caddy doesn't support "y" for this field).
global_opts.validation_cert_lifetime: Enter a Caddy duration such as 90d or 2160h ("y" is not supported here)
global_opts.renewal_window_ratio_help: Fraction of the certificate's lifetime that must remain before Caddy attempts renewal (0-1, default ~0.33). Applies globally, including to hostname-scoped proxies that don't set their own.
global_opts.storage_root_help: Overrides where Caddy stores certificates and other TLS state. Leave blank to use Caddy's own default ($XDG_DATA_HOME/caddy, or /var/lib/caddy under systemd). Changing this does not move existing certificates — Caddy will re-request them at the new path.
global_opts.storage_not_writable: This path isn't writable by Caddy, so it was not saved: {{error}}
global_opts.metrics_enabled_help: Turns on request-level metrics (requests, status codes, durations) across every proxy, plus a small dedicated site that serves them. Go runtime/process metrics are always included by Caddy — there's no toggle to remove those.
global_opts.metrics_listen_address_help: Where the metrics endpoint is served, e.g. ":2019" (all interfaces) or "127.0.0.1:2019" (localhost only). The admin API here runs on a Unix socket, so metrics can't share it — pick a free TCP port.
global_opts.metrics_listen_address_required: A listen address is required while metrics are enabled
global_opts.metrics_listen_address_invalid: Enter a listen address like ":2019" or "127.0.0.1:2019"
global_opts.metrics_plain_format: Use plain Prometheus format instead of OpenMetrics
global_opts.metrics_plain_format_help: Maps to Caddy's disable_openmetrics option. Slightly less verbose output — doesn't remove any metrics.
global_opts.runtime_log_note: This is Caddy's own startup/reload/error log — separate from per-site access logs configured on each proxy. Caddy's default (nothing set below) sends it to stderr, which systemd captures in the journal.
global_opts.runtime_log_enable: Override Caddy's default runtime log destination
global_opts.trusted_proxies_note: If Caddy sits behind another reverse proxy, load balancer, or CDN, it otherwise sees that intermediary's IP as the client IP — this affects access logs and the remote_ip route matcher. Applies to every server; a port with its own HTTP/3 or timeout override still gets this setting merged in separately.
global_opts.trusted_proxies_enable: Trust upstream proxy headers for the real client IP
global_opts.trusted_proxies_ranges_help: Space-separated CIDR ranges, or the private_ranges keyword (all private IPv4/IPv6 ranges) — e.g. from your CDN's published IP list.
global_opts.trusted_proxies_ranges_required: At least one range (or private_ranges) is required
global_opts.trusted_proxies_headers_help: Space-separated header names to check, in order. Leave blank for Caddy's own default (X-Forwarded-For only).
global_opts.trusted_proxies_strict_help: Use when the header might contain untrusted, attacker-supplied entries before the trusted ones — reads from the right instead of the left.
global_opts.proxy_protocol_note: For a TCP-level load balancer that doesn't terminate TLS or add HTTP headers (e.g. AWS NLB, HAProxy in TCP mode) — this replaces the need for Trusted proxies above, which relies on an HTTP header a TCP-level LB can't add. Applies to every server; a port with its own HTTP/3 or timeout override still gets this setting merged in separately.
global_opts.proxy_protocol_enable: Accept PROXY protocol on incoming connections
global_opts.proxy_protocol_allow_help: Space-separated CIDR ranges allowed to send PROXY protocol headers — restrict to your load balancer's own IPs to prevent client IP spoofing. Leave blank to accept from any source.
global_opts.proxy_protocol_timeout_help: Max time to wait for the PROXY protocol header before giving up (Go duration, e.g. 2s). Leave blank for Caddy's own default.
global_opts.on_demand_rate_deprecated: Caddy no longer recommends interval and burst. Clear both and rely on the ask endpoint instead.
global_opts.issuer_local_certs: Caddy's own CA for every site
global_opts.default_sni_help: The server name Caddy assumes when a client sends none.
global_opts.default_bind_help: Space-separated addresses that sites without a bind option listen on.
global_opts.admin_off_help: The plugin needs the admin API to read and change the running configuration.
global_opts.admin_address_help: Where Caddy's admin API listens, written as in the Caddyfile. The plugin connects to the address in its own setting, so change both together.
global_opts.admin_origins_help: Space-separated hosts that may call the admin API from a browser.
global_opts.metrics_per_host_help: Adds the requested host to each request metric, so sites can be told apart. Every distinct host becomes its own series.

ca.title: Internal Certificate Authority
ca.not_in_use_title: No proxies are using the internal CA
ca.not_in_use_body: None of your sites uses the internal CA, so this certificate is not the one presented to visitors: public sites get Let's Encrypt/ACME certificates through automatic HTTPS. This window only shows Caddy's built-in internal CA, used by the "Caddy's internal CA" HTTPS option.
ca.install_instructions_title: How to install in browsers / OS
ca.firefox_instructions: Open Firefox → Settings → Privacy & Security → Certificates → View Certificates → Authorities → Import. Select the downloaded .pem file and check "Trust this CA to identify websites".

acme.title: ACME / Let's Encrypt
acme.intro: Caddy's automatic HTTPS needs no configuration — any hostname below with no explicit policy is silently getting a Let's Encrypt certificate from Caddy's built-in defaults.
acme.empty_body: No hostnames were found: sites use either plain HTTP or Caddy's internal CA.
acme.value_default_ca: (none set — using Let's Encrypt's production endpoint)

admin_address.title: Admin API Address
admin_address.storage_note: These settings are saved in your browser's local storage — they apply only to this browser and are not shared with other users or browsers.
admin_address.tcp_help: Host and port of the Caddy Admin API (default: http://127.0.0.1:2019)
admin_address.socket_help: Path to the Caddy Admin API Unix socket, used as fallback when TCP fails (default: /run/caddy/admin.socket)
admin_address.test_tcp_fail: TCP connection failed — check address and ensure Caddy is running
admin_address.test_socket_fail: Unix socket unreachable — check path and socket permissions
admin_address.container_help: Name or ID of the Docker container running Caddy, used to show logs when Caddy has no local systemd service (optional)
admin_address.test_container_fail: Container not found or not running
admin_address.docker_host_help: Socket of the Docker daemon running the container, e.g. unix:///run/user/1000/docker.sock for rootless Docker. Leave empty for the default daemon
admin_address.test_docker_socket_missing: Docker socket not found — check the path and that the Docker daemon is running
admin_address.test_docker_socket_unreadable: Docker socket can't be read — check its owner and permissions

forward_auth.heading: Forward Authentication
forward_auth.field_url_help: Base URL of the authentication service (e.g. http://localhost:9091)
forward_auth.field_uri_help: Path to request on the auth service (e.g. /api/authz/forward-auth)
forward_auth.field_copy_headers_help: Space or comma-separated response headers to copy from the auth service to the upstream request (e.g. Remote-User, Remote-Groups)
forward_auth.validation_uri_required: Auth URI is required when an auth service URL is set
forward_auth.field_copy_headers_rename_help: Write Name>Other to copy a header under another name.
forward_auth.field_header_up: Request headers to the auth service
forward_auth.field_header_up_help: One per line: Name value sets a header, +Name value adds one, -Name removes one.
forward_auth.field_trusted_proxies_help: Ranges whose X-Forwarded-* headers are kept on the request to the auth service, separated by spaces. private_ranges stands for the private networks.

tls_policy.heading: TLS Policy
tls_policy.cipher_suites_help: Leave all unchecked to use Caddy's secure defaults. Only ECDHE AEAD ciphers are shown (Caddy's supported set).
tls_policy.curves_help: Leave all unchecked to use Caddy's defaults
tls_policy.client_auth_mode_help: Require clients to present a certificate
tls_policy.trusted_ca_file_help: Path to a PEM file containing the CA certificate(s) used to verify client certificates (e.g. /etc/caddy/certs/ca.pem).
tls_policy.cert_lifetime_help: How long internal-issuer certificates stay valid before renewal (default 12h). Use a Caddy duration, e.g. 90d, 365d (Caddy doesn't support "y" for this field).
tls_policy.renewal_window_ratio_help: Fraction of the certificate's lifetime that must remain before Caddy attempts renewal (0-1, default ~0.33).
tls_policy.validation_duration: Enter a Caddy duration such as 90d or 2160h ("y" is not supported here)
tls_policy.hostless_global_only_note: This proxy has no hostname, so Caddy can't scope a certificate policy to it alone. Set the certificate lifetime and renewal window for hostless proxies once, for all of them, in the Global Options tab under "Internal TLS (hostless proxies)".
tls_policy.custom_cert_help: Path to a PEM file with your own certificate (full chain — leaf plus any intermediates). Leave both this and the key file blank to use Caddy's automatic ACME/internal-CA issuance instead.
tls_policy.custom_ca_help: For your own reference only — Caddy has no separate slot for this on a manually-loaded certificate, so any intermediates must already be included in the certificate file above.
tls_policy.custom_file_unreadable: File not found or not readable by Caddy's user
tls_policy.custom_cert_lifetime_note: A custom certificate is loaded above — certificate lifetime and renewal window don't apply, since Caddy isn't issuing anything itself.
tls_policy.acme_email_help: The account email for this site's certificates. It only applies to automatic HTTPS; empty uses the global one.
tls_policy.acme_ca_help: Where this site gets its certificates, for example the Let's Encrypt staging URL while testing. Empty uses the global CA.
tls_policy.acme_invalid_email: Enter an email address such as admin@example.com.
tls_policy.acme_invalid_ca: Enter an http:// or https:// URL.

error_handler.heading: Custom error handlers
error_handler.field_file_root_help: Caddy will serve {status_code}.html from this directory (e.g. /var/www/errors/404.html)
error_handler.replace_upstream: Also replace the app's own error pages
error_handler.replace_upstream_help: Without this, the handlers only answer errors Caddy itself raises (upstream down, no route). With it, error responses from the app (a JSON 404, a 401 asking for a login) are replaced too.

matchers.heading: Route matchers
matchers.field_header_value_help: Leave value blank to match any request that includes the header.
matchers.exclude_help: A request that matches all of these fields is skipped, even when it matches the fields above. Set only these to match everything except them.
matchers.expression_help: A condition that must also be true, with placeholders like {path} or {method}. Caddy checks it when you save.
matchers.ip_kind_client_help: The visitor's IP, taken from the forwarded header when the request comes through one of the trusted proxies (Settings). Without trusted proxies it is the same as the connection IP.
matchers.ip_kind_remote_help: The IP of the TCP connection. Behind a proxy or CDN that is the proxy's address, not the visitor's.
matchers.regexp_help: A name makes the groups available as {re.name.1}, for example in a rewrite. Caddy allows one regex per matcher.
matchers.file_help: Matches when one of the files exists. Placeholders such as {path} work.
matchers.vars_help: One per line: a placeholder, then the values it may have, for example {host} example.com www.example.com.

named_route.help: Also registers the route under a name, so other routes can reuse it with invoke <name>.

servers.field_https_help: A server only listens on ports, so it can't get an automatic (ACME) certificate. Unchecked, it serves plain HTTP.
servers.delete_confirm_body: All routes in this server will also be removed.
servers.field_key_help: Unique identifier (no spaces). Used as the Caddy JSON key.
servers.field_listen_help: Enter port number (e.g. 443, 8080). Add multiple ports to listen on all of them — all routes apply to each.
servers.validation_key_format: Key must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, and hyphens
servers.validation_key_duplicate: A server with this key already exists
servers.validation_addr_required: At least one listen address is required
servers.confirm_add: This will create a new named server block in /etc/caddy/conf.d/. Caddy will need a reload to pick up the new configuration.
servers.confirm_edit: This will update the server block in /etc/caddy/conf.d/ and the Caddy JSON configuration.
servers.no_routes: No routes yet. Add one using the buttons above.

errors.port_used_by_standalone: Port {{port}} is already used by a standalone proxy. Remove it first or use a different port.
errors.port_used_by_server: Port {{port}} is already used by server "{{server}}".
errors.port_used_by_server_add: Port {{port}} is already used by server "{{server}}". Add routes to that server tab instead.
errors.log_file_not_writable: Log file "{{path}}" isn't writable by Caddy: {{error}}
errors.path_outside_sandbox: The caddy service is sandboxed (systemd ReadWritePaths=) to only: {{allowed}}. "{{path}}" falls outside all of them, so Caddy would never be able to write there regardless of file permissions — choose a path under one of the allowed directories, or add this path to the unit's ReadWritePaths= via "systemctl edit caddy".

tls_mode.label: HTTPS certificate
tls_mode.acme_help: Caddy gets and renews a public certificate. The name must point to this server, and ports 80 and 443 must be reachable from the internet.
tls_mode.internal_help: Signed by Caddy's own CA: browsers only trust it where that CA's root certificate is installed. Good for internal names.
tls_mode.acme_needs_name: Signed by Caddy's own CA. Automatic certificates need a public hostname in the host field.
tls_mode.off_help: The site is served over plain HTTP.
tls_mode.on_demand: On-demand: get the certificate at the first TLS handshake
tls_mode.on_demand_help: For names that aren't known in advance. Set an ask endpoint under Settings → On-demand TLS, or anyone who points a name at this server can make Caddy request a certificate for it.

snippets.body_help: Caddyfile directives, as they would appear inside a site block. Saving checks the whole configuration first.
snippets.error_rename_in_use: Snippet {{name}} can't be renamed while these sites import it: {{sites}}
snippets.imports_help: Each snippet is added to the site block as an import line.
snippets.intro: Reusable Caddyfile blocks, such as security headers or basic auth, that sites pull in with import.
snippets.name_help: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
snippets.name_invalid: Use only letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
snippets.save_failed: Caddy rejected the snippet. The previous version was kept.
snippets.settings_from_snippet: Some settings come from snippet {{names}}. Caddy applies them, but they aren't shown or changed here.
snippets.title: Snippets

dns.global_enabled: Use the DNS challenge for ACME certificates
dns.global_enabled_help: Needed for wildcard certificates and for hosts not reachable on ports 80/443. Caddy proves control of the domain with a DNS record it sets through your provider's API.
dns.no_modules_body: The DNS challenge needs a Caddy build with a DNS provider module (dns.providers.*), which distribution packages usually don't include. Use a Caddy build with the module for your DNS provider. This plugin doesn't install one: replacing the packaged binary breaks package updates.
dns.credentials_help: Values are kept in /etc/caddy/dns.env (root only, mode 600) and reach Caddy as environment variables; the Caddyfile only references them. A saved value is never shown again.
dns.value_keep: Saved; leave empty to keep it
dns.validation_option: Option names use letters, digits and underscores.
dns.validation_duplicate: Each option may appear only once.
dns.validation_value: Enter a value for each new option.
dns.restart_needed: Restart Caddy to load the changed DNS credentials. A reload isn't enough: the service reads its environment only when it starts.
dns.site_override: Override: own provider for this site
dns.site_inherit_help: Uses the DNS provider set under Settings → DNS challenge, or the HTTP challenge when none is set.
dns.site_override_help: This site uses its own DNS provider and credentials. Saving new credentials restarts Caddy, because it reads them only when it starts.
dns.site_wildcard_warning: Wildcard certificates need the DNS challenge. Set a DNS provider for this site, or one under Settings → DNS challenge.

tree.aria_label: Route and handle blocks of the site
tree.unreadable: The blocks of this site could not be read as a tree. Edit them in the raw editor.
tree.read_only_help: The route and handle blocks of this site, as written. Read-only for now: edit them in the raw editor.
tree.matcher_help: A path such as /app/*, an @name, or empty for every request. A handle_path needs a path.
tree.saved: The blocks of the site were saved.
tree.block_not_found: The site's block was not found in the Caddyfile. Reload the page and try again.
tree.edit_help: Select a block to change its matcher or its directives, or add, move and remove blocks. Only what you change is rewritten; blocks the form does not know are shown as written, stay read-only and can be moved or removed.
tree.remove_confirm: Remove this block and the {{count}} blocks inside it?

encode.heading: Compression
encode.help: Used while compression is on in General. Without choices Caddy compresses with gzip and zstd.
encode.minimum_length_help: Responses with fewer bytes than this are sent as they are. Caddy's default is 512.
encode.invalid_number: Enter a whole number of bytes.
encode.match_status_help: Space-separated codes or classes such as 2xx 404. Empty means every status.
encode.invalid_status: Enter status codes like 200 or classes like 2xx.
encode.match_headers_help: One per line: the header name, then its value. Wildcards such as text/* work.
encode.invalid_header: Each line needs a header name and a value.

dynamic_upstreams.heading: Dynamic Upstreams
dynamic_upstreams.help: Look the upstreams up in DNS. The target above is the fallback when a lookup finds nothing. Several sources are combined.
dynamic_upstreams.validation_name: A source with settings needs a name.

bind.label: Bind addresses
bind.help: The addresses this site listens on, separated by spaces, for example 127.0.0.1 ::1. Empty listens on every address. A host that is one IP address already binds to it.
bind.invalid: Enter IP addresses or host names, without a port.

modules.title: Caddy modules
modules.unknown: The modules of this Caddy could not be read: neither the caddy command nor the Admin API answered.
modules.help: What the installed Caddy can do beyond a stock build. A feature that needs a missing module fails when Caddy loads the config, so check here first.
modules.non_standard: Modules that are not part of Caddy itself: {{count}}
modules.probed: This Caddy is only reachable over the Admin API, which has no list of modules. Each feature was tested by adapting a small config; only common DNS providers are tested.
